title: CoSLight: Co-optimizing Collaborator Selection and Decision-making to Enhance Traffic Signal Control

problem.claim: Effective collaboration among multiple intersections is important for reinforcement-learning-based traffic signal control to alleviate congestion.

gap.claim: Existing work mainly selects neighboring intersections as collaborators, although non-neighbor failures to collaborate can cause substantial or wide-range congestion.

contributions.claim: A second learned policy separates collaborator selection from signal control and updates concurrently with the original signal-controlling policy.
The selection policy adaptively chooses teammates in real time using phase-level and intersection-level features.
Code is available for the approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets reportedly provide robust validation of the approach's superiority.
The approach reportedly achieves significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-intersection collaboration is important for reducing congestion in reinforcement-learning-based traffic signal control.
Prior work mainly uses neighboring intersections, leaving non-neighbor collaboration failures associated with substantial congestion.
The approach learns a separate collaborator-selection policy alongside the original signal-control policy.
The authors report improvements on synthetic and real-world datasets over existing state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: Non-neighbor intersections may contribute to wide-range congestion when they fail to collaborate.

interpretation.claim: Collaboration mechanisms should not assume that spatial proximity alone identifies the most useful coordination partners.

application.claim: In multi-agent control, consider learning partner selection from task-relevant state features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when non-neighbor selection is preferable or how selection behaves under different traffic conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, optimization procedure, or policy-update details.
The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported improvements.
